headline: Highest risk is data leakage from kotaemon’s broad network/API handling into Superset’s allowlisted analytics path; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts, and Superset is a downstream analytics system that can consume outputs. A shared filesystem is not documented, so I cannot claim a direct bridge; however, the pair still plausibly allows instruction-like content to flow from kotaemon into Superset-rendered artifacts or dashboards. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs untrusted HTML or transcript text into a Superset-ingested dataset, injection content can propagate.
IF Superset renders kotaemon-produced text without sanitization, attacker instructions may be displayed as trusted content.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of raw HTML/MHTML from kotaemon into Superset.
Add a sanitization step for all kotaemon outputs before dashboarding.
Require manual review for any text fields that may contain instructions.
Use separate workspaces for source documents and analytics outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to distinguish data from instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, while Superset has allowlisted egress and can expose analytics outputs. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair creates a plausible path for sensitive document content or secrets to move from kotaemon into Superset reports and then out through networked analytics workflows. Because the exact bridge is undocumented, I choose high rather than medium.
conditions: IF kotaemon indexes documents containing API keys or confidential transcripts and Superset queries that dataset, leakage is possible.
IF Superset exports dashboards or query results derived from kotaemon content, sensitive data can leave the original boundary.
mitigations: Exclude secrets-bearing fields from kotaemon ingestion.
Restrict Superset datasets to redacted or aggregated views.
Rotate any API keys that may have been indexed by kotaemon.
Audit exports from Superset for sensitive columns.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level access controls between the systems.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show shared filesystem paths or locking, so I cannot assert a hard write collision; still, overlapping mutable state and concurrent operation make conflicts plausible in default deployments. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same underlying workspace or database, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF an operator runs multiple kotaemon instances against shared storage, state corruption becomes more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate storage directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared dataset.
Serialize updates through one operator-owned queue.
Back up shared state before running both systems.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can generate citations and answers, and Superset is a BI tool that may render or act on those outputs. The profiles do not prove Superset automatically trusts kotaemon, but the interaction pathway exists if kotaemon-produced summaries are imported as authoritative analytics content. That is enough for medium, not low, because downstream misinterpretation can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards are populated from kotaemon-generated summaries without review, incorrect facts can cascade.
IF operators treat kotaemon citations as verified source data, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human verification before importing kotaemon outputs into Superset.
Mark all imported text as untrusted provenance.
Compare key facts against original source documents.
Limit automated actions based on dashboard content.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for cited claims.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and document content, while Superset’s docs-only profile shows no special regulated-data handling or residency mismatch. There is no direct evidence of a jurisdictional or certification conflict between the pair, so only a small compliance gap is plausible. I do not cite both agents beyond their documented data surfaces because the issue is primarily kotaemon-side handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is loaded into kotaemon and then exported through Superset, retention or access-policy mismatches may occur.
IF the operator requires a specific certification boundary not present in either profile, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Classify and exclude regulated fields before ingestion.
Set short retention on exported analytics artifacts.
Document which datasets may flow into Superset.
Review access logs weekly.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
